advice:
Own verdict: Yes—use a task-changeset binding in existing project records, not a separate ledger. Essential: scoped writer, exact base/head, handoff/recovery, independent diff acceptance, integration provenance, and integrated-result review. Worktree paths are temporary locators, not durable identity.
Gemini review: Agree that persistent paths are redundant and concurrent base advancement is the strongest falsifier. Qualify its SHA recommendation: recording the integrated SHA alone cannot establish that the reviewed revision was integrated; changed revisions require renewed review.
Next: Define lifecycle transitions and invalidation rules; run the three ordered nonauthor design passes; pilot two tasks touching a shared interface, forcing a post-review rebase, and check that stale approval blocks integration.
Risk: Stop if synchronization requires a duplicate ledger or integration can proceed with approval bound to an obsolete diff.

Verdict: Approve the task-changeset pattern; bind integrated tree/commit SHA (essential) rather than persistent worktree paths (redundant after handoff).
Evidence: Northstar mandates reusing project records, single-writer scopes, and reviewing the integrated result while forbidding app specs or duplicate ledgers.
Risk: Concurrent tasks advancing the base branch can invalidate a reviewed commit before integration; falsify by running two parallel tasks requiring a post-review rebase on shared interfaces.
